trajectory_messages.content:
I'm working with Astro files and running the linter with the rule that suggests converting regular imports to type-only imports.

*   When linting an Astro file with the useImportType rule enabled, a component import must NOT be flagged for conversion to a type-only import if that component is referenced as a JSX element in the Astro file's template section (the markup area after the closing frontmatter delimiter).

*   JSX component usage in the Astro template section (e.g., using an imported identifier as a rendered element tag) must be recognized as a value-position reference, preventing the useImportType rule from incorrectly suggesting the import be converted to a type-only import.

*   When the useImportType rule is applied to an Astro file where a component import is used both in a type context in the frontmatter (such as via typeof in a generic type argument) and as a JSX component in the template, linting must complete with no diagnostics and no fixes applied.

*   Linting an Astro file with experimentalFullSupportEnabled and the useImportType rule must produce the output 'No fixes applied' when all component imports are correctly used as rendered elements in the template section.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

## Summary

I fixed a bug in Biome's `useImportType` lint rule where component imports rendered as JSX elements inside an Astro template's text expressions were incorrectly flagged for conversion to type-only imports.

### Root cause

When linting Astro (and Vue/Svelte) files, template code is extracted into embedded JS/TSX snippets, and value-position references in those snippets are tracked so the `useImportType` rule knows an import is used as a value. That tracking happens in `EmbeddedValueReferences::visit_non_source_snippet` (in `crates/biome_service/src/workspace/document/services/embedded_value_references.rs`).

That function only walked for `JsReferenceIdentifier` and `JsStaticMemberExpression` nodes. JSX element names are represented by a distinct node type — `JsxReferenceIdentifier` — so a component rendered inside a template text expression (e.g. `{items.map(i => <Component />)}`) was never recorded as a value reference. If that same component was also referenced in a type position in the frontmatter (e.g. `Foo<typeof Component>`), the rule concluded it was type-only and suggested `import type`.

Top-level template tags like `<Component />` were already covered separately via `visit_html_root`, which is why the plain case worked but the JSX-in-expression case didn't.

### Fix

Added a branch in `visit_non_source_snippet` to handle `JsxReferenceIdentifier`, recording its name as a value reference. Because the base identifier of a JSX member name (`<Ns.Item />`) is itself a `JsxReferenceIdentifier`, walking every occurrence covers both simple and member component names.

### Verification

- Reproduced the failure with a dev build (`Foo<typeof Component>` + `{items.map(i => <Component />)}` was flagged), confirmed it's now clean after the fix.
- Confirmed genuine type-only imports are still flagged (no false-negatives).
- All existing tests pass: `biome_service` unit tests (4), `handle_astro_files` (30), `handle_vue_files` (45), `handle_svelte_files` (25), `vue_cross_language_rules` (4).

No files in `tests/` were modified.
